text:
Predicates:
PerformsOften(x) ::: x performs in school talent shows often.
Attends(x) ::: x attends school events.
Engaged(x) ::: x is very engaged with school events.
Inactive(x) ::: x is inactive and disinterested member of the community.
ChaperonesHighSchoolDances(x) ::: x chaperones high school dances.
Student(x) ::: x is a student who attends the school.
Wishes(x, y) ::: x wishes to further her academic career and educational opportunities.
YoungChildOrTeen(x) ::: x is a young child or teenager.
Bonnie ::: Bonnie.

Premises:
∀x (PerformsOften(x) → Attends(x) ∧ Engaged(x)) ::: If people perform in school talent shows often, then they attend and are very engaged with school events.
∀x (ChaperonesHighSchoolDances(x) → ¬Student(x)) ::: If people chaperone high school dances, then they are not students who attend the school.
∀x (Inactive(x) ∧ CommunityMember(x) → ChaperonesHighSchoolDances(x)) ::: All inactive and disinterested members of the community chaperone high school dances.
∀x (YoungChildOrTeen(x) ∧ Wishes(x, academicCareers) ∧ Wishes(x, educationalOpportunities) → Student(x)) ::: All young children and teenagers who wish to further their academic careers and educational opportunities are students who attend the school.
BonnieAttendsAndEngaged ∧ BonnieStudent ∨ ¬(BonnieAttendsAndEngaged) ∧ ¬(BonnieStudent) ::: Bonnie either both attends and is very engaged with school events and is a student who attends the school, or she neither attends and is very engaged nor is a student who attends.

Conclusion:
(ChaperonesHighSchoolDances(Bonnie) ∨ (¬ChaperonesHighSchoolDances(Bonnie) ∧ PerformsOften(Bonnie))) → (YoungChildOrTeen(Bonnie) ∧ Wishes(Bonnie, academicCareers) ∧ Wishes(Bonnie, educationalOpportunities) ∧ Inactive(Bonnie) ∧ CommunityMember(Bonnie))
